item.title: ‘100 percent a catch’ – NFL fans call out crucial referee decision as Bills beat Chiefs
item.description: Photo by Timothy T Ludwig/Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs lost a close game against the Buffalo Bills on Thanksgiving Day, and fans aren’t pleased with a big decision by the referees during the game’s final moments. The NFL’s final Thanksgiving Day game went right down to the wire, with the Buffalo Bills beating the Kansas City Chiefs 13-10. In a game that was played in tough weather conditions, the Bills won in dramatic fashion with a walk-off field goal from Tyler Bass. Right before that, though, the Chiefs got the ball deep in their own half twice in the dying moments of the fourth quarter. Both opportunities resulted in punts, but the first one was meant to be different. After Patrick Mahomes completed a pass to Rashee Rice on third down to move the chains, the referees then overturned the decision. This had a huge impact on the game, and fans online couldn’t believe it. NFL fans think that Rashee Rice’s catch was actually good and are unhappy it got overturned The referees are always an easy target for fans, but it is frustrating to see their decisions effectively decide close games. Had the Chiefs gotten the first down there, as the initial on-field ruling stated they did, it would have been a huge momentum swing in their favour. It could have changed the result. Instead, the officials ruled that the ball touched the ground when he came down with it. The replays show that it may have been mighty close, but a lot of fans think they got it wrong. “That’s a catch. The NFL has no idea what a catch is anymore,” one fan claimed. “That was 100 percent a catch, what is wrong with these refs, man?” a second fan asked. “Guess it doesn’t have to be conclusive anymore. Honestly have no idea what these refs are doing at this point,” said a third fan. “It’s a catch… Notice how they conveniently didn’t have the conversation about the balling hitting the ground with the receiver maintaining control. A conversation they have ALL the time in this scenarios,” a fourth fan pointed out. “Textbook catch. NFL saving their golden boy once again,” a fifth fan commented, taking a shot at Josh Allen. “Seems kind of ridiculous. He had full control of the ball. It never moved,” a sixth fan pointed out. Whether it was a catch or it wasn’t, the bottom line remains unchanged. The Bills have officially become the first team this season to win 10 games. As for Kansas City, they have now fallen behind the Denver Broncos in their division. They will need to bounce back from this result as quickly as they can. item.title: Ex-champion boxer Linares released by US immigration authorities
item.description: Jorge Linares, who has been detained by US immigration agents, celebrates his WBA lightweight title win over Mercito Gesta in 2018 (JEFF GROSS) Former world boxing champion Jorge Linares has been released by United States immigration authorities, the president of the World Boxing Association said. The 41-year-old Venezuelan, a three-division world champion, said on November 15 that he had been detained in El Paso, Texas. "Our friend and former WBA world champion Jorge Linares is back with his family," Gilberto Mendoza posted on X Wednesday. News of Linares's detention came via his social media and was later confirmed by US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). He had been facing deportation proceedings. "This is crazy," Linares had written on X. His lawyers said at the time that he "is authorized to be in the United States and he has cooperated fully with immigration authorities." Linares, who is widely regarded as one of the most skilful fighters of his generation, won world titles at featherweight, super featherweight and lightweight during a 21-year career. Nicknamed "The Golden Boy," he won his first world title in 2007. He retired in 2023 following defeat to Britain's Jack Catterall in Liverpool, finishing his career with a record of 47 wins, 29 by knockout, and nine defeats. burs-pnb/pst

item.title: Knicks’ win streak doesn’t stop Mike Brown from being blunt about team: ‘We haven’t arrived’
item.description: Mike Brown isn’t letting his Knicks team get comfortable. They have responded emphatically to their shaky start to the season — after losing their first three games of the year, the Knicks have gone 12-3. They have won six in a row and are tied for second in the Eastern Conference ahead of their game against Giannis Antetokounmpo’s Heat Friday night at Madison Square Garden. They are starting to resemble the team that finished last year with a championship. But Brown holds the same sentiment he did during those first few games. Mike Brown reacts on the sidelines during the Knicks’ win over the Cavaliers on Nov. 25, 2026, at Madison Square Garden. Jason Szenes for New York Post “Our s–t still does stink,” Brown said. “We haven’t arrived. We still have to embrace the little things and all those things. We may do this [go up], but eventually we’re gonna do this [go down]. When we do that, handling the challenges in front of us is gonna be big. You can’t get too high in this league because you’re that close to going the other way. Just like if you’re down, it’s not the end of the world, you’re that close to flipping it. You try to be even-keeled.” Friday’s game is the Knicks’ fourth and final NBA Cup group-stage game. And they face an uphill battle to defend their title. To win their group and advance to the knockout rounds, they need to beat the Heat by at least seven points and have the 76ers lose to the Pacers. Advancing as a wild-card team is much more complicated and far more unlikely. The Knicks lost their first two group-stage games to the 76ers and Pacers, respectively, before beating the Cavs on Wednesday. Friday will be the first time they face Antetokounmpo with the Heat . He has been battling a groin ailment but is listed as probable to play. OG Anunoby, who has missed the past three games due to a left calf strain, is doubtful for Friday’s game. That is a slight improvement, as he was ruled out for Wednesday’s win over the Cavs from the start. Jordan Clarkson, who has missed the past four games with right plantar fasciitis, is questionable — also an improvement after being ruled out of Wednesday’s game from the beginning. Miles McBride, who has missed the past two games due to left adductor tightness, is questionable. Andre Drummond, who injured his head during Wednesday’s game, is questionable as well.

item.title: What ‘people inside the Steelers’ have told Jay Glazer about the Aaron Rodgers drama after he was cut
item.description: Photo by Franco Arland/Getty Images Aaron Rodgers has officially been waived by the Pittsburgh Steelers. The quarterback has dominated headlines this week after being dropped for the game against the Denver Broncos. He then had a go at his coach, Mike McCarthy, which led to the Steelers cutting him just hours later. Everyone who follows the NFL has had an opinion about the drama, but what is the feeling inside the Pittsburgh Steelers? Jay Glazer says nobody is happy. People inside the Pittsburgh Steelers are not ‘thankful’ for the Aaron Rodgers situation Controversies within a team are never a good sign, and the whole situation with Rodgers is no different. We’re sure the quarterback’s teammates all hold him in high regard for everything he has achieved in the game, but his recent outburst puts everyone in a difficult position. McCarthy, general manager Omar Khan and owner Art Rooney are all on the same page and have made the decision to cut Rodgers. That shows whose side they are on, but the feeling within the organisation is still not a good one, even though the saga is now over. That’s according to NFL insider Glazer, who revealed on Fox Sports: “I got so many messages. And really, the predominant message I got was, ‘This is sad.’ “When you talk to people inside the Steelers, it’s supposed to be Thanksgiving; nobody is thankful that this is going on.” There was probably no way back for Rodgers after his comments on the Pat McAfee show, accusing McCarthy of showing up late and even falling asleep during quarterback meetings. However, the main tipping point was the ultimatum the 42-year-old reportedly laid out to his head coach, saying that if the system doesn’t change to how he wants, he would request his release. It really is a shame that things have unfolded this way for the Steelers, especially on Thanksgiving week, but the drama is finally over. The focus for the Steelers should now be on how they move forward, with Mason Rudolph set to take Rodgers’ place in the team. Prior to this injury stint, which sidelined him for three games, Dorofeyev had six goals and six assists in his first 21 games as a Ranger . The 26-year-old was still in the process of finding his groove with the team that signed him to a seven-year, $77 million deal this past offseason. While Dorofeyev and his linemates had been able to generate multiple scoring opportunities, the Russian wing struggled to actually find the back of the net. It prompted Sullivan to try Dorofeyev in different spots within the top nine , as well as in different positions on the power play. The injury disrupted it all, but it’ll be interesting to see how Sullivan utilizes Dorofeyev upon his return and if he can bridge the disconnect he’s had on offense. item.title: Andy Reid gives 2 injury updates after loss to Bills
item.description: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - OCTOBER 25: Trey Smith #65 of the Kansas City Chiefs looks on before the game against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field on October 25, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. The Seattle Seahawks won 20-3. (Photo by Alika Jenner/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs only officially ruled one player out of Thursday’s sloppy 13-10 loss to the Buffalo Bills . Wide receiver Jalen Royals left the game with an ankle injury in the second half. The second-year pro was quickly ruled out . Then, in the fourth quarter, right guard Trey Smith was seen heading into the locker room in frustration. The team never provided an update on the two-time All Pro selection, but he appeared to suffer a similar injury to Royals. “As far as the injuries go,” said head coach Andy Reid after the game, “Jalen Royals hurt his left ankle. He sprained it. Trey Smith likewise.” Tight end Travis Kelce took a frightening hit to the back in the second quarter but stayed in the game and led all Chiefs receivers with four catches for 71 yards. The Chiefs will play a second consecutive Thursday night game in Week 13 when they travel to face the Los Angeles Rams. We will watch for updates on Royals and Smith — and players such as running back Kenneth Walker and tackle Jaylon Moore who did not play against Buffalo — when the team releases its first official injury report on Monday.

item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Aaron Rodgers’ tenure with the Pittsburgh Steelers came to an ugly end this week after he was benched, unloaded on head coach Mike McCarthy, and was released. Plenty of people around the NFL have weighed in, and now one of Rodgers’ biggest rivals has joined them. Tom Brady addressed the saga during Fox’s Thanksgiving coverage, and while he praised Rodgers as a Hall of Fame player, he made it clear that he didn’t like how the quarterback handled his exit. Brady said that the locker room is “a very sacred place” and that private matters shouldn’t become public. Rodgers’ Ugly Exit With the Steelers on a two-game losing streak, McCarthy benched Rodgers on Tuesday night and named Mason Rudolph the starter for Friday’s game against the Denver Broncos. Rodgers, who played for McCarthy for 13 seasons in Green Bay, reportedly gave McCarthy an ultimatum before the move. Rodgers then called into The Pat McAfee Show on Wednesday and went scorched earth on his former coach. He claimed that McCarthy fell asleep in meetings, missed walkthroughs, and ended a halftime speech with “one, two, three, go Packers!” something McCarthy apparently confirmed , and the Steelers released him later that day. On Thursday, Steelers owner Art Rooney II backed McCarthy with “100% confidence” and said Rodgers wasn’t being a good teammate by going public. Former Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin also weighed in on Thursday night, calling the situation “a dumpster fire” during NBC’s halftime show. ‘A Very Sacred Place’ Brady, who played against Rodgers for nearly two decades, echoed Rooney’s point that some things should stay behind closed doors. “Yeah, and that’s one thing I just think in response to that, the sanctity of an NFL locker room is a very sacred place and we shouldn’t ever lose track of that as players. It’s a privilege to be in that locker room. You’re fighting with your teammates, you’re fighting with your coaches, you’re always acting as a team together and shouldn’t always be the place for, you know, private things to become public. That’s what I’ll say,” Brady said, on Fox . When Brady’s broadcast partner pointed out that this could be the way Rodgers’ career ends, Brady was quick to praise his longtime rival. “Certainly. item.description: LaMelo Ball clutched his left ankle in pain and went to the locker room in the final minutes of Wednesday's win over the Oklahoma City Thunder . He rolled it as he landed on Isaiah Hartenstein, giving the Minnesota Timberwolves a real scare. They lost superstar Anthony Edwards for an extended period after he underwent arthroscopic surgery on his right knee. Minnesota has thrived without Edwards, with several players stepping up. Ball dusted off his No. 1 option cape to lead the team; Jaden McDaniels is on a scoring tear , and Ayo Dosunmu is saving the day in clutch moments. Coach Chris Finch acknowledged the reality of missing another star player. Finch said he must determine who to replace Ball in the starting lineup if he misses time. Finch May Rely on Two-Way Players David Banks-Imagn Images The Timberwolves coach said the team may activate their two-way players. Zyon Pullin could see on-court action as the lone guard, as Johni Broome and Rocco Zikarsky are big men. Pullin had an impressive outing in the preseason finale against the Chicago Bulls in 38 minutes. He recorded a double-double, scoring 14 points on 3-for-9 shooting (8-for-10 from the free-throw line) and 10 assists. Minnesota's two-way guard favors attacking a rotating defense to either draw a foul or hit a dump-off pass to a teammate under the basket. Those passes are going to Rudy Gobert and Joan Beringer. His aggression also led to a 22-point outing against the Miami Heat . The team will need his ability to punish rotating defenses and create quality looks for his teammates. The simple, effective passes will suffice for Finch, especially coming off the bench with Dosunmu and McDaniels taking on heavier ball-handler duties in the starting lineup. Ball’s Long History With Ankle Injuries Alonzo Adams-Imagn Images Ankle injuries have been Ball's Achilles' heel throughout his career. It's likely part of the reason the Charlotte Hornets traded him after his first healthy season. item.title: The Galaxy keep missing the playoffs. Fans want ownership to take action
item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. However, general manager Will Kuntz , speaking in a videoconference with the media Friday, agreed things are dismal. “I don’t think we did a good enough job collectively last year,” he said. “So for us, it’s really about taking a hard look at everything we’ve done process-wise and saying ‘hey, how can we be better?’ Because it cannot continue like this.” Galaxy coach Greg Vanney reacts during a match against LAFC at BMO Stadium on Oct. 25. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. Getty Images The head coaching role will take on an even bigger role going into 2027 as NYCFC prepares for massive changes with the planned move into their new stadium and MLS changing their league calendar to a summer-through-spring format, which is in line with the European football calendar and includes an abbreviated sprint season that will run from February to May. The club views this next year as a “crucial point in franchise history” and the feeling is that NYCFC wants to make sure it has “the right leadership in place,” the source added. NYCFC will begin its search for a new head coach immediately, sporting director Todd Dunivant said in a statement released late Sunday morning. “We would like to thank Pascal for his commitment and contributions to New York City FC and wish him and his family all the best. This decision follows a thorough review of the season and reflects our ambition as an organization,” he said. One of the biggest problems that NYCFC faced this season – especially during its struggles in the second half – had been allowing late goals that would cost the club points, or matches altogether. And the club dealt with a number of injuries during the course of the season, while also playing much of the year without one of its top scorers, Alonso Martinez, as he recovered from a torn ACL he suffered last fall. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
